- (c) The time output lines that were generated by the prior experiments included not only elapsed time, but also user and system processor times. If you add together the user and system processor times to get total processor times, you should find that the total is in each case quite similar to the elapsed time, because the `threads` program kept the one processor busy essentially the full time. Now suppose you switch to using two processors. With normal CFS scheduling, what do you expect to happen to the total processor time as the number of threads goes from 1 to 2, 3, and 4? Why? To test your prediction, run the following commands:

```

```
